messages:
mira: Heads up — after enabling kernel auto-select (FlashAttention preferred) we saw p95 token latency regressions on short-chat traffic (~16-64 tokens). Not a capacity issue, looks like kernel swap overhead + paged-KV page faults.

alex: Ack. Can you paste the perf trace and a sample request pattern?

mira: Quick dump — two consecutive small-seq requests. trace shows kernel switch + KV page load between them.

mira: ```
req1: seq=48, kernel=FashAttn, kv_resident=false, kernel_switch_us=0
req2: seq=12, kernel=SmallSeqKernel, kernel_switch_us=1250, kv_page_faults=3, addl_latency_us=1800
stack: runtime->kernel_selector->load_page->swap_kernel
```

jonathan: Ugh. So the selector flips kernels per-request which causes device context thrash and paged-KV thrashing. Two levers: 1) prefer stable kernel for N requests (sticky), 2) prefetch likely KV pages when switching.

sam: Agree. For sticky kernel we already have a token-budget threshold but defaults were aggressive. What if we use a queue-level token budget instead of per-request? e.g., form a micro-batch until budget 256 tokens or 25ms. That keeps kernel steady for the batch.

kevin: I prototyped queue-budget sticky behavior: keep kernel pinned for a queue until either budget_exhausted or time_window expires. Local tests: p95 improved ~6-9% for mixed short/long. But tail still suffers when page faults occur.

perf-bot: perf_snapshot: p50=12ms, p95=78ms (baseline), after-budget-pin: p50=11ms, p95=71ms, page_fault_rate=-12%

alex: Nice. What prefetch heuristics did you try for paged KV? async load first N pages when kernel switch predicted?

kevin: Tried simple prediction: if next request <64 tokens then don't change kernel; if >64 then switch and async prefetch next 3 pages. Prefetch cut page-fault latency by ~900us on avg. But prefetch increases memory bandwidth — watch heavy-long seq traffic.

mira: We should trade off prefetch vs. memory pressure. Proposal: queue-level policy that records recent transition cost per model variant and chooses sticky or switch based on amortized cost vs latency benefit. Keep config flags: sticky_threshold_tokens, sticky_time_ms, prefetch_pages, prefetch_concurrency.

jonathan: +1. Also add a fast-path: if KV is resident (small working set), allow kernel swap without prefetch. We can detect residency via a cheap bloom filter of hot pages.

sam: Who wants to own a small RFC? I'll draft a short design and perf plan. Targets: p95 reduce by >=7% on mixed workload, page-faults drop >=10%, no >2% regressions on all-long workloads.

mira: I'll attach the trace snippets and a reproducer (local loadgen config) to the RFC. For reproducer: two streams, 70% short(12-48), 30% long(128-512), concurrency 40.

ops-bot: Reminder: please add a canary rollout with kernel-select telemetry flags and fallback to previous selector on +10% latency regression within 1h.

kevin: Will send patch for queue-budget sticky + simple prefetch toggle tomorrow. I'll include perf harness results and run against staging.

alex: Thanks — sync in daily stand after patch. If we need, we can also experiment with micro-kernel that covers 8-64 tokens to reduce swaps.

mira: TL;DR: immediate mitigation = queue-level token budget + sticky kernel pinning; medium = prefetch + hot-page bloom filter; long = micro-kernel and refined selector cost model.

sam: :thumbsup:
